claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 19 and still lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son named Alex who is 19 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is over 16, there are specific rules that apply. You can still qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying A-levels, doing a college course, or in an apprenticeship?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is still in education - he's doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is 19, still living at home with you, and is in approved education (doing A-levels), this supports your eligibility.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex - meaning you live with him and/or contribute to his upkeep (things like food, clothes, pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here with me and I take care of all his needs - food, clothes, everything really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. One final important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 19 years old and is in approved education (doing his A-levels), which qualifies under the rules for children aged 16-19
- He lives at home with you in the UK
- You are responsible for him and provide for all his needs
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important things to keep in mind:**

1. **If Alex finishes his A-levels**: You'll continue to receive Child Benefit until he either leaves education, turns 20, or starts working 24 hours or more per week.

2. **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay a tax charge. This doesn't affect your eligibility, but you may want to consider whether to claim or not.

3. **Notify HMRC if circumstances change**: You should inform HMRC if Alex stops his education, starts working 24+ hours per week, or any other relevant changes occur.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit online or by post. If you need any more information, feel free to ask!
